It turns out that the verticies of our iNObodies from Theorem 1.1 and Theorem 1.2 happen exactly when there is a change in the associated base loci of the graded linear series W•t. These ideas are generalized by the authors in [FL25b] on any projetcive variety X by connecting three aspects of local positivity of a line bundle L on X at a point x ∈ X. On one hand we have inﬁnitesimal successive minima, then jets and ﬁnally polytopal upper and lower bounds on the generic iNObodies. Moreover, in [FL25c] the authors study the shape of generic iNObodies on Jacobians in small dimensions. The main issue here is realizing at least asymptotically the family W•t as complete graded linear series on a modiﬁcation of Pn−1. For example, for non-hyperelliptic Jacobian threefolds, W•t becomes complete on a birational model of P2 that is far from being toric, while for the hyperelliptic case we may need to go to the Zariski–Riemann space.

For box-products of arbitrary degrees the vertical slices of ∆x(L) are still a family of NObodies on XΣ with respect to general linear ﬂags. But it is harder to guess the vertices. It seems an interesting problem to ﬁnd an algorithm that starts with a polytope in Rn−1 that is a NObody on a toric variety with respect to a T-invariant ﬂag, and construct another polytope, that will be a NObody on the same toric space but with respect to a generic linear ﬂag.
In both cases, the shapes degenerate to the simplex in Theorem 1.1 when di = 1 for all i, while when the di are not all equal the shapes are not simplicial.
In dimension n 3, we can ﬁnd non-trivial sections on XΣ, whose valuations provide the vertices of a slice of the global NObody on XΣ with respect to general linear ﬂags. More precisely: Theorem 1.2. pretation of the family of graded linear series W•t. When X = C1 ×...×Cn, intersection theory on BlxX implies that W•t is contained in a family of complete linear series associated to divisors on XΣ, the blow-up of Pn−1 in n points in general linear position. We show that this inclusion is asymptotically an equality. For this we use that XΣ is a toric variety and the asymptotic behaviour of complete linear series on them can be managed through convex geometry. As a consequence, the vertical slices of ∆x(L) are NObodies associated to a ray of divisors on XΣ with respect to a generic (strict transform) linear ﬂag. Lastly, the global (gluing all t 0) NObody on this special ray of divisors on XΣ is exactly the convex set described in the statement, as we are able to prove the existence of sections whose valuation are the vertices of the simplex.
